name: inkie-deck-workspace
description: Workspace root for Inkie Deck, a web control plane for a fleet of AI agents, and the bundled agent protocol package it is built on
_comment:engines: The lowest version that satisfies every engines.node in the installed tree AND sits on an LTS line still receiving security patches. The strictest real constraint is jsdom's ^20.19.0 || ^22.13.0 || >=24.0.0; nothing in the tree needs more than 22.13.0. The old >=22.18.0 had no justification in the history, and written that way it also admitted Node 23, which was never an LTS line and is already end of life. Enforced by engine-strict in .npmrc: without that, this field is advisory and a Node 20 machine installs, typechecks, tests and gates clean.

scripts._comment:run: A bare-machine run stopped dead here. A reader finishes the README, has every check green, and has no next line to type: the runnable scripts live in packages/deck, and `pnpm dev` at the root answered `Command "dev" not found`. Knowing that a pnpm workspace means `cd` into a subdirectory is developer knowledge, and this project's readers are not all developers. These three forward the naive guesses to where they actually live.
scripts._comment:test: One workspace at a time, deliberately. pnpm -r defaults to running package scripts in parallel, and the base suite drives bin/create-agent.sh as real subprocesses. Run alongside deck's suite, that load alone pushed a dozen of deck's 5-second per-test timeouts over the line: 64 failures, none of them a real defect, on a tree that is green when the two run in sequence. A suite that fails for load reasons is no more use than one that passes for environmental ones.
